svg.text: one vocabulary for every architecture diagram — a shape or colour means the same thing on every page
COMPONENTS · reuse these, never redraw them
chunk — the unit of parallelism, retry and resume
record chip — the op type travels with the row
selection — fewer leave than entered (never a
GLYPH TEMPLATE · pick from these, don't invent a new icon
one glyph per concept, 24 px, in the hue of the block it sits in — the same set is in the shape library
INTERFACES · HLD notation for the code-shaped parts
an interface box lists real method names with (); a ball means “implements” and a socket means “uses”
a worked example beats an abstract box
1 One meaning per shape and colour — on every page, without exception.
2 Flow reads left → right; stacks read top → bottom. Never both at once.
3 Solid = data, dashed amber = state, bold green = commit. Label arrows with verbs.
4 Real values in every shape: ctid ranges, LSNs, id 2 · Bob. Never lorem boxes.
5 Vendor marks identify systems; the shape still carries the meaning.
6 ≤ 12 primary nodes per page. Split rather than shrink the type.
7 Every page: a title, one-sentence caption, and numbered steps if order matters.
8 A new concept gets its symbol added to this page first.
Edit freely — this page is the contract every other page keeps.
